description: Scans reader-facing claims for certainty-implying language ("(verified)", "independently verified", "guaranteed", "fact-checked", "100% accurate", ...) that isn't backed by an appropriate provenance tier, plus tiers that require a sourceRef but don't have one, and claims carrying an unrecognized tier. Run it on any copy, marketing page, or AI-drafted content that makes factual-sounding claims before it ships. The default phrase list is a short starter list (11 phrases), not a taxonomy -- it will miss phrases it doesn't know about: compliance attestations ('SOC 2 certified', 'HIPAA-ready'), superlatives ('best-in-class') and 'clinically proven' all pass; extend `certaintyPhrases` for your domain. Phrases match as word prefixes (from the start of a word, with no end boundary), so a custom phrase 'proven' also reports 'provenance' (but not 'unproven'): list the exact words you mean and review each hit. The check does not read context: a limits statement such as 'Concurrent renames are outside this guarantee' is still reported for 'guarantee'. A negation word ('not', 'without', ...) suppresses a match only inside the same clause (a comma, semicolon, period, colon, !, ?, em or en dash, or line break ends it; a plain hyphen does not), after the last 'and'/'but', and within `negationWindow` characters. It is a window, not a parser, so it can still suppress an overclaim the negation does not govern. An empty result means no wording offenses were found under the configured rules; it does not verify the claims.

certaintyPhrases.description: Override the certainty-phrase vocabulary. Defaults to a generic starter list ('(verified)', 'independently verified', 'proprietary dataset', 'guaranteed', 'fact-checked', '100% accurate', ...).

anyOf.description: A bare phrase to scan for.

reason.description: Why this phrase asserts certainty, surfaced in offense messages.

certaintyRequiresTier.description: Tiers strong enough to back certainty language. Default ['verified'].

id.description: Stable identifier for the claim (slug, DB id, DOM id).

sourceRef.description: Pointer to what backs the claim (URL, doc citation, record id).

text.description: The claim text exactly as it would be shown to a reader.

tier.description: 'verified' = checked directly against the source's own published material. 'modeled' = an estimate derived from public signal, explicitly not a measurement or guarantee. 'editorial' = stated judgment/opinion.

negationWindow.description: Maximum characters before a phrase match to scan for a negation word ('not', 'without', ...), cut off at the start of the clause. Default 40.

requireSourceRefForTiers.description: Tiers that must carry a visibly non-empty sourceRef (not only whitespace or invisible characters). Default ['verified'].

name: check_provenance_claims
title: Check claims for unbacked certainty language
